name: First turn
challenge: Turn the orange ring until its gap reaches the hook. A ring with nothing left to hold shatters.

name: Held
challenge: Only the last ring turns: the others are held by their own arms. Start at the end of the chain.

name: Flower
challenge: Three petals hook the center. One long turn of the center frees them all at once.

name: Swing
challenge: Free the small ring, then the middle ring carries its arm. One way the arm hits the hook above; turn the other way.

name: Bridge
challenge: The middle ring is closed and cannot let go of anything. Free both sides; it shatters when nothing holds it.

name: Make way
challenge: The right ring cannot finish: its arm runs into the arm of the left ring. Turn the left ring first to clear the path.

name: Slide out
challenge: Two bars run into the gaps of the top and bottom rings, so those rings cannot turn. The frame on the right is in the way of both bars: slide the frame out first, then each bar, then turn the rings.

name: In the way
challenge: The bar runs into the top of the middle ring and can only slide up and out, but the ring above is in its way. Clear the top ring, slide the bar out, then open the middle ring.

name: Two at once
challenge: A bent bar runs into the gaps of the hub and of the lower ring, so neither can turn. It slides out along its pins, but the short bar above is in its way: slide that one up into its ring and out first.

name: Workshop
challenge: Three bars hold three rings. The bent bar cannot slide out while the long bar is in its way, and the long bar cannot slide up while the top ring sits on its path. Clear the top corner, slide the long bar, then the bent bar, then open the hub.

name: Ladder
challenge: Each ring of the ladder has a bar run into its gap. Slide the rungs out (the middle one needs the side ring turned first), then take the ladder down from the top.

name: Knot
challenge: The bar runs into the gap of the right ring, but a ring hooks the bar, so the bar cannot slide (a knot). Turn the bomb ring up into the bar: the blast clears the bar, then the right ring can turn.

name: Aim
challenge: Two rings sit beside the bomb ring. The right one can be freed by turning it; the closed one on the left cannot. Send the bomb left.

name: Long way
challenge: Free the small ring, then turn the bomb ring. The short way runs the bomb into its own pin; go the long way round to the knot.

name: Scales
challenge: Two bars run into the side rings, and each bar is hooked from above, so neither can slide (two knots). Each bomb ring must turn up into its own bar; turned the other way, its bomb hits the center ring instead and the level is lost.

name: Ring road
challenge: Breather: around the road, two rings hold each other and neither can turn. Clear the road up to the bomb ring and send its bomb into the pair.

name: Key
challenge: The blue ring is locked: a tap only shakes it. Free the yellow ring that carries its key, then the blue ring turns.

name: Key bar
challenge: The key of the locked ring is on the bar that runs into the left ring. The right ring is in the bar's way: turn it first, slide the bar out, then the lock opens.

name: Key chain
challenge: Three rings in a triangle: the top one holds the key of the left, the left one the key of the right. Open them in order.

name: Vault
challenge: The bomb ring is locked; its key is on the bar run into the left top ring. The right top ring is in the bar's way, and its pendant must go first. Slide the bar out, then aim the bomb at the closed knot ring, not the free one.

name: Wave
challenge: A bent bar runs into the tops of the left and middle rings, another into the bottoms of the middle and right rings. Slide each one out, both legs at once, then open the rings.

name: Gears
challenge: Turn one gear and its partner turns the other way. Find the direction where both gaps reach their pins.

name: Drawbridge
challenge: The bridge is a bent bar in the tops of both gears, so the gear pair cannot turn. The ring above is in the way of the bridge: clear it, lift the bridge out, then one turn of the gears frees both pendants.

name: Partner
challenge: The orange gear looks free but only shakes: its partner still hooks the purple ring. Free purple first, then turn the pair the way that keeps the free arm off the pin.

name: Gear train
challenge: Three gears turn as one, the middle one the other way, but the middle gear is locked. Get its key from the top chain. The bomb on the right gear must reach the closed knot below before the gears let go of their pins: one direction does both, the other wastes the bomb.

name: Nest
challenge: Breather: small rings sit inside big ones and hook their inner side. Turn the big rings so their gaps pass the inner hooks.

name: Crossfire
challenge: Each bomb ring sits next to the wrong knot: the near hit is on a free ring. Clear the bar first so each bomb can reach across.

name: Clock
challenge: Four small gears sit around a big gear. Two clock hands are bars run into two of the small gears, so nothing can turn. Slide both hands out, then one turn of the big gear moves all four small gears the other way.

name: Lift
challenge: The key sits on a gear pair, and a bar runs into each gear. Slide both bars out, turn the pair to drop the key, then the locked cabin ring and its chain can move.

name: Grid
challenge: Nine rings in a grid, linked like a maze, a locked center, and two bent bars run into the four corner rings, with a ring above and below in their way. Clear those, slide the frames out, then find the one corner that starts the chain.

name: Branches
challenge: Breather: a branching tree. Every leaf is free; clear the leaves and the branches follow.

name: Safe
challenge: The bomb ring is also the key holder: when it explodes the lock opens. Unlock the cover first, then blow the knot, then free the cover.

name: Mirror bomb
challenge: The bomb rides the right gear, which turns opposite to the gear you drag. Aim it at the closed ring below, not the free ring above.

name: Tower
challenge: A tower of gears and bars. The roof is a bent bar in the tops of both gears, and it holds the key of the base. Climb down: roof, gears, base.

name: Fortress
challenge: Two bomb rings are locked, their keys on the two gate bars run into the gear pair. Slide each gate out, then aim each bomb at its own knot; each has a free decoy on the other side.
probs: K2 (#16) starts inside the gap of R7 (#7), so it is free at once.

name: Snake
challenge: Breather: a long snake of rings. Start at the tail and follow it to the head.

name: Cage
challenge: A big ring cages three small ones. Two hook its inner side and hold it; a bar runs from the gap of the third, out through the gap of the cage. Slide the bar out first, then turn the cage past both inner hooks and the hook below.

name: Gear bridge
challenge: Four gears in a row turn as one, each the other way from its neighbour. Bars run into gears 1 and 4; a bomb rides gear 3. Slide both bars out, then choose the one direction that sends the bomb into the knot below, not the free ring above.

name: Spiral
challenge: Rings wind in a curl, smaller to the end. The inner end is locked and its key is the outer end ring. Unwind it in order.

name: Crown
challenge: Finale: two bars run into the gear pair, the jewel is locked with its key on the left bar, and the bomb ring at the base has a decoy on the near side and the hook of the jewel blocking the far side. Bars, then gears and jewel, then send the bomb the long way to the knot.
